person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how subjective confidence in a choice relates to the value comparison that produced it, in behaviour and in the brain
span.quote: Decisions are never perfect with confidence in one’s choices fluctuating over time. How subjective confidence and valuation of choice options interact at the level of brain and behavior is unknown.

span.label: whether confidence is a read-out of noise in the value comparison, separable from the value difference itself
span.quote: In contrast, the field of perceptual decision-making has highlighted the fact that confidence can be measured independently of the choice process itself 9 , 10 , where it is conceptualized as reflecting a “second-order” metacognitive evaluation. Critically, dissociating confidence from other features of the decision process requires acquisition of separate measures of choice and confidence

span.label: dissociates confidence from value difference, shows a race model explains their joint relation to accuracy and reaction time, locates both in vmPFC, and predicts individual metacognitive ability from vmPFC-rRLPFC coupling
span.quote: Our findings provide a mechanistic link between noise in value comparison and metacognitive awareness of choice, enabling us both to want and to express knowledge of what we want.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Here we show that decision confidence emerges from a value-comparison process in vmPFC, and that this region is in turn accessed by rRLPFC to enable a subjective assessment of confidence.

span.label: decision confidence in value-based choice
span.quote: Here we implement such an approach to dissociate value and confidence during decision-making, and to identify their respective neural substrates.

span.label: fmri
span.quote: Scanning acquisition was performed using a Siemens 3.0 Telsa Allegra MRI Scanner (Erlangen, Germany).

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: This model predicts that subjective confidence reflects the stochastic accumulation of evidence during the value comparison process.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: The intuition is that, even within a particular level of initial DV, inter-trial noise in the value comparison process results in some trials having greater final DV’s (higher confidence) than others.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: One computationally plausible hypothesis is an hierarchical model where confidence in a comparison process is “read out” by an anatomically distinct second-order network

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: Intuitively, if reported confidence is a noisy facsimile of the confidence inherent in a decision process, the relationship between confidence and behavior will weaken, and metacognitive accuracy will decrease 26 .

span.label: in the race model confidence is the gap between the two accumulators when one crosses threshold, so it tracks trial-to-trial noise rather than the starting value difference
span.quote: We adapted a race model 7 , 21 wherein evidence in favor of each option (the snacks presented on the left and right side of the screen) is accumulated over time and the decision is made on the basis of the first option to reach a threshold ( Figure 2b ). In this model confidence is defined as the absolute difference between the two accumulators at decision time (Δe).

span.label: the same noise makes a trial faster, more accurate and more confident at once, which is why the three covary without any of them causing the others
span.quote: The intuition is that, even within a particular level of initial DV, inter-trial noise in the value comparison process results in some trials having greater final DV’s (higher confidence) than others. Such decisions will tend to be made more quickly, be more accurate, and be associated with higher confidence

span.label: because confidence follows the stochastic path rather than the initial difference, the model itself explains why value and confidence come apart
span.quote: Finally, since the model predicts that confidence reflects the stochastic evolution of a value comparison process, it will only be weakly related to initial DV. This feature of the model provides a parsimonious explanation for why DV and confidence are dissociable in our behavioural data.

span.label: a second-order region reads confidence out of the comparison process, and how faithfully it does so varies between people
span.quote: An additional parameter (σ conf ) governs the noise in the read-out of Δe (i.e. decision confidence). If σ conf is zero the information about confidence (Δe) is uncorrupted, resulting in a pronounced shift in the choice accuracy between high confidence and low confidence trials (red arrow). As the level of metacognitive noise increases (more positive values of σ conf ) the shift between the two curves (low and high confidence) diminishes. Differences in σ conf account for the inter-subject variability in metacognitive reportability we observed behaviorally.

span.label: Only a small, experimentally controllable subset of the factors that could influence confidence was measured.
span.quote: Here we report a limited set of these factors (see Supplementary Table 1 ) for which we could exercise good experimental control.

span.label: The design cannot adjudicate between confidence emerging in vmPFC and confidence being computed elsewhere and fed into vmPFC; that would need a high-temporal-resolution method such as MEG.
span.quote: Resolving this possibility is beyond the design of the current study and will require other techniques with high temporal resolution, such as MEG, that can track the evolution of confidence and valuation in the brain.

span.label: Alternative functional mappings from model confidence to reported confidence were not explored.
span.quote: We note that other functional forms for the link between model confidence and reported confidence are possible, but we do not investigate these here.

span.label: the authors state that only a limited set of the factors affecting confidence could be controlled
span.quote: We recognize that aside from ∣DV∣ and RT other factors (internal and external) are likely to affect subjective confidence. Here we report a limited set of these factors (see Supplementary Table 1 ) for which we could exercise good experimental control.

span.label: the direction of the vmPFC-rRLPFC relation is not resolvable by fMRI; confidence could be computed elsewhere and imported
span.quote: An alternative interpretation of our data is that information about choice confidence is coded elsewhere, perhaps in parallel to the construction of choice values, and is then communicated to vmPFC (possibly via rRLPFC) where it is incorporated into the choice process. This mechanism would be analogous to a modulation of the vmPFC value signal during self-control by dlPFC 31 . Resolving this possibility is beyond the design of the current study and will require other techniques with high temporal resolution, such as MEG, that can track the evolution of confidence and valuation in the brain.

span.label: 8 of 28 participants were excluded, including one for not varying their confidence ratings enough to estimate the measure of interest
span.quote: Participants were only included if they used a sufficient range of confidence ratings (standard deviation > 0.8) to allow estimation of metacognitive ability. This criterion led to the exclusion of one further subject.

span.label: value is measured after scanning by a separate bidding task, so choice and value come from different sessions
span.quote: To establish value for individual items we asked participants at the end of the scanning session to place a bid for each food item using a standard incentive compatible procedure, the Becker–DeGroot–Marschak (BDM) mechanism 15 . span.label: the race model, imported from perceptual choice into value-based choice

span.label: confidence here is NOT risk: every option has a known outcome, so this is certainty about having picked the better item, not uncertainty about what will happen
span.quote: Note that confidence, or certainty, in the present study is conceptually distinct from risk, in that each choice determines a known outcome. Confidence here reflects the degree of subjective certainty in having made the best choice, which equates to choosing the higher valued item.

span.label: choice confidence (second order, about the comparison) versus bid confidence (first order, about each item's value) - two senses of one word, measured separately and adjudicated by model comparison
span.quote: This analysis confirms that a critical modulator of choice accuracy is 2 nd level confidence arising in the context of the comparison process ( Model 2 ) as opposed to 1 st level confidence in the item values ( Models 3 - 5 ).

Together these results indicate that confidence is a stable predictor of choice accuracy, and does not reflect local changes in attention.
